user.title: Xolta battery (local Modbus)
user.description: Enter the IP address of the Xolta site controller. Give it a fixed IP address (DHCP reservation) in your router first. Modbus TCP must be enabled by Xolta/Ebbefos support; see the README for the e-mail to send.

data.allow_write: Allow Home Assistant to control the battery

data_description.host: The fixed IP address of the site controller, e.g. 192.168.1.50.
data_description.allow_write: Off = read only (safe). On = adds an override (Auto / Stop / Self-consumption) that writes to the battery. You can change this later under Configure.

data_description.host: The new fixed IP address of the site controller.

error.cannot_connect: No answer from this address on port 502. Check the IP address and that Home Assistant can reach it.
error.connection_refused: The controller refused the connection. Modbus TCP is probably not enabled yet; ask Xolta/Ebbefos support to enable it (see the README).
error.not_xolta: Something answered, but it does not look like a Xolta site controller.

abort.already_configured: This controller is already set up.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The IP address has been updated.

data.allow_write: Allow Home Assistant to control the battery
data.repeat_interval: Repeat interval while an override is active

data_description.allow_write: Turning this off removes the override entities and stops any active override. Nothing is written; the cloud takes control back by itself.
data_description.scan_interval: How often the battery is read. Default 10 s.
data_description.repeat_interval: The cloud resets the mode after about 90 s, so the override is written again at this interval. Default 20 s.

set_override.name: Set override
set_override.description: Start or end a battery override. Auto writes nothing; the cloud takes control back within a few minutes.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Hours before Auto is restored. Default: the Override duration entity.

write_failed.message: Could not write to the battery: {error}
